name: MSP / IT support trial sequences (the client's offer to the client's prospects)
source: Copy v2 (docs/research/v2-leads-copy.md): Sequence T structure (plain text, no links in email 1, one reply CTA, four touches) with four proven frameworks. Wording is new and makes no claim about the client beyond {oneLiner} / {proof}; the client reviews it on the approval page.

problem-first.label: Problem first
problem-first.why: Names the everyday IT pain small offices live with, then one line on the offer, then an interest question (30MPC: leading with the problem +20 % replies).

touches.subject: @variant

touches.body:
{FirstName}, one more thought.

When something breaks at a small office, the fix is rarely the real cost. The real cost is the half day your team loses waiting.

Worth a short call to see if {ClientCompany} could take that off your plate?

touches.subject: IT at {Company}
touches.body:
{FirstName}, a different angle.

Picture your main computer or email going down tomorrow morning. Many {ICP} would not know who to call first.

That is the gap {ClientCompany} fills.

Would a 15-minute call next week be useful?

{FirstName}, this is my last note so your inbox stays clear.

If IT support comes up at {Company} later, a one-line reply here is all it takes.

Should I close the file for now?

question-led.label: Question led
question-led.why: Opens with a neutral question about how they handle IT today (Josh Braun's 'poke the bear'); the reply is easy to write.

touches.subject: @variant
touches.body:
Hi {FirstName},

{FirstLine}

{oneLiner} Many {ICP} lean on a staff member for IT until something big breaks.

Who looks after IT at {Company} today, someone inside or an outside firm?

{FirstName}, asking because the answer tells me quickly whether this is worth your time.

If it is someone inside, {ClientCompany} can take the routine work off their plate. If an outside firm is doing well by you, no need to change.

Which is it at {Company}?

touches.subject: backups at {Company}
touches.body:
{FirstName}, one practical check.

It is worth knowing when someone last restored a file from your backups to prove they work. At many {ICP}, nobody ever has.

Want {ClientCompany} to run that check with you?

{FirstName}, this is my last note so your inbox stays clear.

If IT comes up at {Company} later, a one-line reply here is all it takes.

Should I close the file for now?

quick-idea.label: Quick idea
quick-idea.why: Gives one small, useful idea before asking for anything (value first); the ask is to send a short outline, not a meeting.

touches.subject: @variant

touches.body:
{FirstName}, a list like that is quick to write and easy to put off.

{ClientCompany} can draw it up with you and keep it current.

Would that be useful for {Company}?

touches.subject: IT at {Company}
touches.body:
{FirstName}, a second idea.

The machines everyone relies on each day are usually the ones nobody has checked in a while. A short review often finds two or three quick fixes.

Open to {ClientCompany} doing one for {Company}?

{FirstName}, this is my last note so your inbox stays clear.

If IT comes up at {Company} later, a one-line reply here is all it takes.

Should I close the file for now?

local-proof.label: Local proof
local-proof.why: Leads with one true proof line the client gave us (30MPC: social proof +41 % replies). Used only when the profile has a proof line; never invented.
